object_types.name: VendorStatus
object_types.definition: The current status of a vendor record.

source_references.excerpt: Draft, active, suspended.

object_types.name: SpendTier
object_types.definition: Procurement-assigned tier reflecting how much is spent with the vendor.

source_references.excerpt: Every vendor has a tier. Bronze, silver, gold.

object_types.name: RiskTier
object_types.definition: Compliance-assigned tier reflecting the risk level of the vendor, set by the review.

source_references.excerpt: I use low, medium, high.
Risk tier comes from the review, so a vendor without a review has no risk tier. Draft vendors don't have one.

object_types.name: RiskReview
object_types.definition: A record of a compliance risk review performed on a vendor; a vendor accumulates review records over time, with at most one being the current signed-off one.

source_references.excerpt: The review is its own record. It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask. It's not a checkbox on the vendor.

object_types.name: ReviewId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier of a risk review record.

source_references.excerpt: It has a review ID, because we need to know who signed it and when, and auditors ask.

object_types.name: ReviewCurrentFlag
object_types.definition: Indicates whether a review is the current signed-off review for a vendor.

source_references.excerpt: A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

object_types.name: ReviewSignedOffFlag
object_types.definition: Indicates whether a review has been signed off.

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review. Not zero, and the one has to be signed off.

ambiguities.description: Tax ID is not a unique identifier for Vendor because subsidiaries share tax IDs and duplicate onboarding occurs, but the transcript does not clarify whether TaxId should be modeled as a shared/non-unique attribute or excluded entirely from uniqueness reasoning going forward, nor how the known duplicate-vendor cleanup project affects the model. Should duplicate vendors eventually be merged, and how should the model represent 'same real-world entity, multiple vendor records' in the interim?

source_references.excerpt: We have vendors with the same tax ID -- different legal entities under one parent that file together, or we've onboarded the same company twice by accident and nobody's merged them.

ambiguities.description: The term 'tier' is overloaded: Dana (procurement) uses it to mean spend tier (bronze/silver/gold) while Raj (compliance) uses it to mean risk tier (low/medium/high). Both are modeled as separate fields, but the team has been unable to enforce distinct naming in practice for two years. Should the system-facing labels be renamed to 'SpendTier' and 'RiskTier' to eliminate ambiguity, and is there any place in the current system where the generic term 'tier' alone is stored ambiguously?

source_references.excerpt: That's not the tier I use. ... We've asked people to say spend tier and risk tier. Nobody does. It's been a losing battle for two years.

ambiguities.description: The relationship between RiskReview and RiskTier/VendorStatus transition is not fully specified: it's stated a completed, signed-off, current review is required for active status, and that risk tier is set 'by the review', but it's unclear whether RiskTier is an attribute of the RiskReview (denormalized onto Vendor) or independently settable. Is RiskTier stored on the Vendor, derived from the current RiskReview, or stored on the RiskReview record itself?

source_references.excerpt: Risk tier comes from the review, so a vendor without a review has no risk tier. Draft vendors don't have one. ... It's set by the review. A vendor with no review has no risk tier.

ambiguities.description: The post-suspension handling of in-flight purchase orders (a potential 'run-off' status) is explicitly unresolved and pending a steering-group/Legal decision. The model currently only captures three vendor statuses (draft, active, suspended) with no representation of in-flight PO behavior under suspension. This is a known gap, not a bug in extraction, but any future model change here needs revisiting.

source_references.excerpt: Then we need a middle state. Something like run-off -- existing POs complete, no new ones can be raised. ... what happens to in-flight purchase orders when a vendor is suspended is undecided.

ambiguities.description: Whether the 'active vendor requires current signed-off review' rule should be modeled as a subset/equality constraint between Vendor-status=active and RiskReview-current+signed-off flags could not be captured directly (ORM constraint types available don't cleanly express conditional constraints across value-restricted states). Should this be expressed as a subset constraint restricted to VendorStatus='active', and is there tooling support for value-scoped subset constraints?

source_references.excerpt: Every active vendor has exactly one completed risk review. Not zero, and the one has to be signed off. ... A vendor accumulates review records over time. At most one is the current one. Being active requires a current signed-off review.

ambiguities.description: Address is mentioned as three distinct addresses (remit-to, ship-from, legal) which are 'frequently different and frequently wrong,' but no further structure, identifiers, or fact types for Address were specified in enough detail to model confidently. Should each address type be a separate value type/fact type, and what is the internal structure of an address (street, city, etc.)?

source_references.excerpt: Address, though we have three addresses really -- remit-to, ship-from, and the legal one, which are frequently different and frequently wrong.

ambiguities.description: Mei's informal spreadsheet includes a 'preferred vendor' flag used when multiple vendors can supply the same item, but this was explicitly declared ad hoc and out of scope for modeling. Confirming this remains excluded: should 'preferred vendor' ever become a formal rule, what criteria would define it?

source_references.excerpt: There's a column called "preferred." It means if two vendors can supply the same thing, buy from this one. It's not in the system anywhere. It's just my column. ... It's ad hoc. Don't model it.

The transcript never gives an explicit contact identifier, so 'contact_id' as reference_mode is an assumption that may need validation.
